qa.q: Study the long profile of a river.
What is the long profile of a river?
qa.a: The long profile is a line that shows the change of the gradient (slope) of a river from its source to its mouth.

qa.q: Name the three courses of a river and the main work of the river in each one.
qa.a: The upper course (vertical erosion), the middle course (lateral erosion and transportation) and the lower course (deposition).

qa.q: Compare the gradient at the source and at the mouth.
qa.a: At the source, the gradient is steep. At the mouth, it is almost flat, near sea level.

sum.title: I. The Long Profile of a River
defs: The long profile of a river is a line that shows the change in its gradient (slope) from the source to the mouth.
items: A. Illustration
The long profile is steep near the source and almost flat near the mouth. It is concave (curved like a slide).
long_profile.png
B. The Three Courses
– Upper course: steep gradient, narrow V-shaped valley, vertical erosion.
– Middle course: gentler gradient, wider valley, lateral erosion and transportation.
– Lower course: almost flat, wide floodplain, deposition.

qa.q: Study the four mechanisms of river erosion.

qa.a: Hydraulic action is the force of moving water hitting the bed and banks. It pushes air and water into cracks and breaks off pieces of rock.

qa.q: What is the difference between abrasion and attrition?
qa.a: In abrasion, the stones carried by the river scrape the bed and banks. In attrition, the stones knock against each other and become smaller and rounder.
Solution is the chemical dissolving of rocks such as limestone by river water.

sum.title: II. Mechanisms of River Erosion
sum.intro: A river erodes its bed and banks in four ways:
items: A. Hydraulic Action
The force of the water hits the bed and banks and breaks off pieces of rock.
river_erosion.png
B. Abrasion (Corrasion)
The load (sand and stones) rubs and scrapes the bed and banks, like sandpaper.
C. Attrition
Stones carried by the river hit each other and become smaller, smoother and rounder.
D. Solution (Corrosion)
River water dissolves soluble rocks such as limestone.

evaluation: What does the long profile of a river show?
It shows the change of the gradient of the river from its source to its mouth.
In which course is vertical erosion dominant?
Vertical erosion is dominant in the upper course.
Why are the stones of a river bed smooth and round?
Because of attrition: the stones knock against each other and lose their sharp edges.
remediation: The start of a river is its ______.
The end of a river is its ______.
The main work in the lower course is ______.
The force of moving water is hydraulic ______.
end.remediationAnswers: 1. source 2. mouth 3. deposition 4. action 5. abrasion 6. attrition
end.homework: Find a photo or a video of the Vina Falls or the Tello Falls near Ngaoundéré, or of the Kola Gorges near Guider. Describe the river and its valley in three sentences.
end.homeworkTag: This prepares Lesson 19: The Upper Course of a River.
teacherNote: Checked: the Benue rises on the Adamawa Plateau, flows through the Lagdo reservoir and Garoua, and joins the Niger at Lokoja (Nigeria). Its length is about 1,400 km.
Around Garoua, the Benue shows middle-course features (wide valley, meanders, sandbanks and braided channels in the dry season).
